Issue https://github.com/shamaton/msgpack/issues/59 (closed completed 2026-05-14 by shamaton) gives source-to-sink Unmarshal*/asInterface -> timeDecoder.IsType -> ext.DecoderCommon.ReadSize1 reading buf[1] on truncated fixext 0xd4-0xd8, panic index out of range. At vulnerable tag v3.1.0 (20ba54b7cb9510db62a97fbe2880d91bd125f8f0) ext/decode.go ReadSize1 is `return (*d)[index], index + rb` with no len check; time/decode.go IsType does `code, offset := td.ReadSize1(offset, d)` then a second ReadSize1 for the type byte on Fixext4/8; internal/decoding/interface.go loops extCoders (default time.Decoder) and calls IsType before any frame-length check. Parent of the true BIC maps a lone 0xd6 through mapLength to errorTemplate rather than reading index 1. This is a real CWE-125 DoS, not a withdrawn advisory.

findings: Real published vulnerability: truncated MessagePack fixext (0xd4-0xd8) reaches timestamp type-sniffing and panics via an unchecked 1-byte read. CVE.org CVE-2026-32284 is PUBLISHED; GHSA-h9q6-hc68-35rp is reviewed and not withdrawn.

Primary introducer_sha 22d35bc1e4ff27db21407bb7e705e06da95dfeea is not the BIC. It copies already-reachable isDateTime/asDateTime logic into ext/ext.go CommonDeseri.ReadSize1 and exttime/time.go; parent 3070a7ac9910c36462553a96a265390dbd11ed63 already calls isDateTime from struct and asInterface paths.

Correct main/v3.1.x BIC is 8c8c814cd610748cf55d233336fb72b9f9c87a77, which first wires isDateTime/asDateTime into deserialize of structs. Immediate parent c2bc01dc6f2f75570a2e7337cc7a78c602c98835 lacks that call and mapLength-errors a lone 0xd6. v2/v3.0.0 equivalent is 01899368db8a658e85398c15eaf7d3020124d6c8.

c136a4310e9a0c64498201d8e199e12a4eae5e3f first inserted unused isDateTime; 025d91a4f4a08a8acb6c5003e45075dad48adcb2 later default-registers the ext timestamp decoder; 30c7746b90336db9c9dc647a5256f0282eaa14fb only refactors the copied readers. None of those is the first reachable write.

PR #32 / 01ee57d9d63a659e59a6257f8dc4cf94ae27b6cf (CVE-2022-41719) added bounds checks to decoder.readSize1 but not ext.DecoderCommon.ReadSize1, leaving the 2026 residual sink. That is incomplete remediation of the 2018 mechanism, not a new first-write.

Fix lifecycle matches the primary: direct member 60a5450f42c21d75a7b17c4cd7074f9ab6065f46, squash 269f54e9483a09dc0c78f0a98c9858337a90d879 in v3.1.1 not v3.1.0, backport d20ec6cfe33e5e7153d6b0d8f4c426ce27942207 in v2.4.1 not v2.4.0. Advisory/OSV rows still say no patched version.
BIC-only attribution is human shamaton with no AI/bot/generator marker on 8c8c814 (and on 22d35bc). Closed verdict stays NOT_AI; primary_verdict is right for the wrong SHA.
